# Best RV power station and solar combo

The right combo depends on how you camp. The search results only gave me one direct purchase link (ALLPOWERS). For the other models, I've linked the review pages that cover them, and you'll need to check current prices at the retailer.

## Weekend or short trips, no air conditioning
**EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024Wh, 1,800W output, up to 1,000W solar input, about 28 lb). It was ranked best overall for camping, and it recharges from AC in about 56 minutes. Its two 500W solar inputs let you add panels later without hitting a ceiling. It can also expand to 5kWh. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is the simpler, lighter option at about 23.8 lb. Its solar input tops out at 400W, so two 200W SolarSaga panels is the useful maximum. Buying more won't charge it faster. ([same review](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

## Boondocking or running the roof AC
**EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** (4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, expandable past 12kWh) was the top RV pick in one comparison. A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500W while running, which is roughly 2.3 hours on one battery. It's heavy enough that moving it is a two-person job. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

**Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** (3,024Wh, 3,000W, 6,000W surge) is the simpler choice if AC is your main heavy load. ([same article](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

## Best value
**BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048Wh, 2,400W, up to 1,200W solar input, built-in 30A RV outlet). It's about 62 lb, so it's a heavy unit for the money. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

**ALLPOWERS R4000** (3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, 2,000W solar input, 5-year warranty, 45 kg/about 99 lb). It lists at $1,499, and code **EXTRA12** takes $179.88 off, bringing it to $1,319.12. Dealectric tested the code on 2026-10-23, and it expires 2026-11-15. The site says stores usually accept one code per order, and the final price is whatever checkout shows. This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission. [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). Reaching the full 2,000W of solar needs panels on all three inputs, since each is limited to 650W. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

## Choosing solar panels
- **Match panels to the station's solar input limit.** Extra panel wattage past the cap is wasted, and one source calls this a common mismatch in van and RV builds. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life))
- **Portable setups:** 200W folding panels such as the Jackery SolarSaga or Renogy 200W suitcase are common pairings. The NomadSignal guide lists the Renogy suitcase as a pairing. ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife))
- **Larger units:** a rooftop or multi-panel array makes more sense for the Delta Pro 3, AC200L, or R4000.

## Caveats
- Most of these sources earn affiliate commissions, and their prices vary. One older comparison lists the Bluetti AC200P at 700W solar input, while the newer AC200L is listed at 1,200W. Check the exact model.
- The EmergencyEnergy article is written for Ontario, Canada. Its electrical-code advice doesn't apply directly in the US, but the specs and AC-load math do. Have a licensed electrician do any hardwired connection to your RV.

## My pick
For most RVers, I'd choose the **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** with 400-1,000W of panels if you don't run the AC off-grid. If you do, choose the **DELTA Pro 3** or **Jackery 3000 Pro**. If you tell me your RV type, daily loads, and budget, I can narrow it to one setup with panel sizing.
